# Route

This file is the process. It is the same in every project and on every machine. The job table is `skills/ROUTE.md` in the repo you are in. That table is the only project-specific part.

Search the table. Do not read it end to end. Take one row.

1. A cell that starts with `node ` is the command. Run it. Open nothing else.
2. A cell that says `none` is a Make. Open the one file that row names.
3. Two When cells still match. Stop and ask. Do not open both.

A task the table does not name is still this process. In the same commit, add one row: when it applies, which file to open, which files to leave closed. A second task that hits the same row replaces the sentence that failed, or adds one trap sentence when that row has none for this miss. The same trap on two rows moves into `skills/shared/<name>.md`, and the rows keep that name. A trap is the command or the refusal. It does not cite an archive.

A better way replaces the old one in the same edit. Delete the sentence, the step, or the row it retires. Add with nothing deleted only when the table had no row. The route changes when When, Open, or Leave closed changed. The how-to changes in the one file that row already opens, and it is not copied into a second skill or an archive. A trap that was already written, and the miss still shipped, is replaced by the check. It is not given another sentence. One miss replaces one instruction. A rejected method is one line, or it is gone. The attempt stays in git.

A script becomes a command cell only when it imports the parts it reuses. A script that draws those parts stays `none`.

A run that followed a `node` cell and matched edits neither the table nor an archive.
